newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended sharply higher on Tuesday, tracking strong markets around Europe, dealers said.
They said the long bond future, close to its record high, was eyeing psychological resistance at 117.
"The only thing to do is to be long in this market," said Emilio Sainz, a trader at Natwest in Madrid.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was little changed at 67 bps.

He said that after the Bank of Spain's decision to hold the key money market rate unchanged at 5.25 percent earlier this morning, the Spanish yield curve flattened as dealers sold the short end and bought the longer end.
The spread between the three-year and 10-year bonds ended at around 133 basis points, down around 10 basis points from yesterday, dealers said.

The Spanish Treasury will auction one-year and 18-months bills on Wednesday, while eyes will also be on the release of first quarter gross domestic product data from National Statistics Institute INE.
